item.title: Come for the science, stay for the big iron: Supercomputer admin on why he loves the job
item.description: Web hosting might seem like an unlikely on-ramp to supercomputer administration, but it set Mark O'Shea on his way to running some of Australia's most powerful machines. O'Shea is team leader for supercomputing operations and senior supercomputing systems administrator at Australia's Pawsey Supercomputing Research Centre . Pawsey is home to Setonix, an HPE Cray EX supercomputer with more than 200,000 AMD EPYC CPU cores and hundreds of AMD Instinct MI250X accelerators. Its GPU partition ranks 87th in the November TOP500 and 37th in the Green500 , which measures computational performance per watt. "Working in web hosting wasn't much different to what I was doing a few years later with supercomputers," O'Shea tells The Register . "Datacenters are essentially several thousand computers, as are supercomputers. "So, we essentially had the same problems," he says, especially as regards cooling and power management. There's no single formal route into supercomputer administration in Australia, O'Shea says. He picked up the necessary skills over time. Andrew Underwood, Dell's chief technology officer for high-performance computing and artificial intelligence across the Asia-Pacific, Japan, and China, says that lack of formal training means some supercomputer admins start in academia. He's observed that many HPC admins emerge from the sciences, catching the computing bug during their studies. A biologist working with a massive genomics database, for example, might discover a taste for running the systems behind it. "The biologist might decide they want to be someone working in IT helping other biologists transform their industry," Underwood says . "One of the things I really admire about people who work in the supercomputing field is they take it so seriously," Underwood adds. "It's almost a passion, a hobby, more so than it is a job." "They want to play that real supporting and foundational role of assisting and engaging with scientists to help them use the technology to solve the problems the world faces." O'Shea agrees, noting that many people who get into supercomputer admin are PhD graduates who stick around their universities after they graduate. Some of them gravitate toward running the departmental computers and then wind up in supercomputing. "There are many roles around universities allowing people to be introduced to [supercomputer administration] while still doing enterprise-style or more departmental admin for researchers and system administration," O'Shea says. Regardless of how a supercomputer admin gets their gig, both O'Shea and Underwood say the supersysadmin community is tight knit – which may not always be a good thing. "As an industry in supercomputing, we need to be open to people from diverse backgrounds," Underwood says, "and we need to build these frameworks like the Student Cluster Competition, conferences like eResearch and the SC Conference, where students can get educated and systems admins get exposed to continual training." item.title: Leeds United head-wrecking crew stay the right side of crazy at Chelsea - Graham Smyth's Verdict
item.description: Leeds United head-wrecking crew stay the right side of crazy at Chelsea - Graham Smyth's Verdict It's good to be just the right side of crazy. More often than not Leeds United Football Club finds itself involved in mayhem. That is an apt word for so much of all that has happened to and around this club since its very inception in 1919. There's been good crazy and bad crazy, everything from the daft to the scarcely believable. Leeds United is a club that rarely needs a second invitation to lose the run of itself. Even under the calm managerial control of Daniel Farke and the sober ownership of 49ers Enterprises, minds have melted and chaos has briefly reigned at times. Take, for example, the last trip to Stamford Bridge, when Leeds lost 6-3. Scorelines like that rarely make sense. That was, in the words of Jayden Bogle, a 'crazy game' and something that he wanted to put right. And what better way to do that than a good old-fashioned historical head-wrecking. It all started with a bit of cat and mouse. Leeds almost played rope-a-dope in the opening stages, seeing relatively little of the football and absorbing pressure. Chelsea saw precious little of James Trafford's goal, because Leeds stayed so compact and patient, looking for opportunities to nip in. Farke's three centre-backs all chipped in with important interventions but almost all of the defending was kept to the edge of the area and further out. It wasn't until the 14th minute that the hosts mustered a shot, Morgan Rogers pulling the trigger from distance and missing the target. Chances to break out were few and far between, but when Leeds did get hold of the ball they moved it well. So well in fact that they created two good opportunities to open the scoring. James Justin's cross from the right was perfect for Dominic Calvert-Lewin and his header was so close to perfect - only the crossbar saved Chelsea. Quick, slick football unlocked space on the left and Noah Okafor's cross was headed downwards by Calvert-Lewin and Emiliano Martinez held on. Having worked so hard to break Chelsea's spell of territorial dominance, conceding an opener will have annoyed Farke. A second source of chagrin was the manner of the concession. One long ball, one lost aerial duel, a missed handball, one pass to the left and a shot seared inside Trafford's near post. The keeper appeared to be well positioned but was simply unable to get a hand on a thunderously-struck shot. Leeds responded to the goal not only with annoyance, but like it was a grievous personal slight. The response was pure manic aggression. The first goal came three minutes after Chelsea's. Calvert-Lewin gave Chelsea a hard time of it in the middle, Okafor joined in and took a pass from the no.9 and then did all the rest himself. Three players put themselves between Okafor and the goal and he still managed to squeeze off a shot with surgical precision, through a defender's legs and into the far corner of the net. item.title: South Carolina football’s Shane Beamer apologizes to fans for 2nd-half performance vs. Georgia
item.description: Matt Pendleton-Imagn Images South Carolina football’s Shane Beamer apologizes to fans for 2nd-half performance vs. Georgia appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . South Carolina head coach Shane Beamer had a blunt message for Gamecocks fans after his team suffered a 34-6 loss to No. 1 Georgia on Saturday. Beamer apologized for his team’s second-half performance, calling it unacceptable after South Carolina failed to keep pace with the Bulldogs. The No. 21 Gamecocks entered halftime trailing just 10-6 at Williams-Brice Stadium, keeping the game competitive through the first two quarters. However, Georgia took control after the break, scoring 24 unanswered points to pull away and spoil South Carolina’s final home game of the regular season. “The second half is just unacceptable,” Beamer said after the loss, according to reporter Matt Dowell. “And I apologize to our fans for the second half. The first half in a lot of ways was our standard. That second half wasn’t our standard. What couldn’t happen tonight happened in the second half.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Shane Beamer after tonight's loss to Georgia: "The 2nd half is just unacceptable. And I apologize to our fans for the 2nd half." @GamecockFB | @wachfox pic.twitter.com/ziB6snoqYg — Matt Dowell (@MattDowellTV) November 22, 2026 Georgia’s offense found its rhythm after halftime, while South Carolina struggled to generate momentum. Nate Frazier scored twice as the Bulldogs capitalized on the Gamecocks’ inability to respond and secured a convincing victory. Additionally, Beamer also credited Georgia and head coach Kirby Smart for their performance, recognizing why the Bulldogs remain at the top of the college football rankings. “Congrats to Kirby and Georgia,” Beamer said. “They’re the number one team in the country for a reason, and they showed it.” The defeat leaves South Carolina at 6-5 overall and 4-5 in SEC play. The Gamecocks now have one regular-season game remaining, with an in-state rivalry matchup against Clemson next week offering Beamer and his team an opportunity to respond. item.title: Macau GP: Kean Nakamura-Berta takes win after Enzo Deligny crashes out
item.description: Motorsport photo Kean Nakamura-Berta claimed a comfortable Macau Grand Prix victory after forcing early leader Enzo Deligny into a mistake at Lisboa. It was a tricky first few corners for the drivers starting on the front row as second-placed Mattia Colnaghi struggled to get away, while polesitter Rashid Al Dhaheri was immediately under attack. Deligny braved it around the outside of the Mercedes junior at Mandarin to grab the lead, before Al Dhaheri then lost out to both Nakamura-Berta and Yuki Sano on the run to Lisboa. Williams junior Nakamura-Berta spent the next couple of laps putting Deligny under pressure before a brief safety car period was triggered when ninth-placed Reza Seewooruthun was tapped into the barriers out of Mandarin by last year's F4 World Cup winner Jules Roussel. Nakamura-Berta continued to remain about half a second behind Deligny upon the restart until he suddenly closed on lap 10 of 16. The SJM Theodore Racing driver was right on the tail of Deligny on the run to Lisboa and the leader left his braking as late as he dared but it was too late and he ploughed into the barriers. This gifted Nakamura-Berta a huge 3.5s lead, which enabled him to stroke it home to the flag to take the victory. The British-born Japanese, Slovak driver, who was third in this year's Formula Regional European Championship standings, made up for the disappointment of crashing out of the F4 World Cup last year. His large margin was aided by R-ace GP driver Al Dhaheri spending several laps bottled up behind Sano's TOM'S Formula Regional machine. The qualification race winner eventually found a way through around the outside of Mandarin on lap 12 but there was too much for him to do to close on Nakamura-Berta in the remaining three tours. Alex Ninovic Alex Ninovic Alex Ninovic made a similar move on Sano at Mandarin on the following lap to return to his starting spot of third on the grid. The 2025 GB3 champion then set about battling Al Dhaheri, blasting ahead on the run to Mandarin on the final lap to finish second, 2.456s behind the winner. Nakamura-Berta's team-mate James Egozi also passed Sano in the closing stages to seal fourth. Sano then lost out to fellow Japanese racer Taito Kato (ART Grand Prix) on the last lap but proceeded to plough into Kato at Lisboa as he attempted to retaliate, with the unsighted Matteo De Palo collecting them. This meant Alex Powell (Prema) and Ernesto Rivera (Van Amersfoort Racing) completed the top six, while Colnaghi was eventually classified 11th after his startline strife. item.title: 'Not the right time' - Fernandes pauses Man Utd contract talks
item.description: Bruno Fernandes has scored in each of his past two games for Manchester United [EPA] Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes says he has been offered a new contract by the club but feels it "is not the right time" for discussions about his future. The 32-year-old midfielder is out of contract at the end of the season , though the club have the option to trigger a 12-month extension until 2028. He was left out of the side under previous manager Michael Carrick but says he has no issues at the club and has chosen to stay at Old Trafford despite offers elsewhere in recent seasons. He told Sky Sports: "The club offered me a new contract, so I think that, from their side, shows that they want me to stay. "There's no negotiations ongoing, but I've seen people saying that 'he's asked for more money, he's asked for more years'. If I wanted more money, I wouldn't be here. "I had somewhere to go to get much more money than being at Manchester United. I could have been in a place that is much warmer than Manchester. "Two summers ago, three summers ago, last summer, I always had the chance to leave and I always chose to be here." United chief executive Omar Berrada recently spoke about Fernandes' contract situation, saying: "It's true that we're having conversations about his new contract, but I prefer to keep that private." Fernandes has scored 75 Premier League goals since signing from Sporting in 2020 and last season set a record for the most assists in a Premier League season. His form has tailed off this season in a poor start for the club as a whole. United are 19th in the Premier League table going into Mauricio Pochettino's first game in charge against rivals Liverpool on Sunday afternoon. "We spoke about the contract at the end of last season," Fernandes said. "We came in at the beginning of this season speaking about the contract, but about the context of the team and the club, I just put that to a side because I don't think it's the right moment, neither for me, nor for the club, to be talking about negotiations. "The most important thing now is that the club gets back to winning games." 'He will see what Man Utd are made of' - Pulis on Pochettino's first game No fallout with Carrick Fernandes was dropped for the Premier League defeat by Bournemouth last month after being critical of United's approach in their heavy defeat against Como in the Champions League. But Fernandes says he did not fall out with Carrick, who was sacked on 12 November. "The manager came to speak to me before the Bournemouth game, to say: 'Look, I'm not going to start you tomorrow. There's nothing to do with the words of Como, I know people will make it around that. I just want to tell you that we need to change something, I need to make a change, performances have not been great, so I just want you to know that there's nothing to do with that'," Fernandes said. item.title: How lessons from football history reveal the real reason behind Manchester City’s decline
item.description: The best part of five hours after the final whistle blew at the Etihad Stadium and about 150 miles north east, Noni Madueke scored an equaliser to ensure the day ended with the equation ultimately unchanged. Manchester City will still go to Arsenal on Sunday six points behind the reigning champions. They could reduce the gap to three, though the evidence of recent weeks is that it is likelier to stretch to nine. That would surely end City’s title challenge. The theory had been that it would take a potential punishment for their 114 guilty verdicts to do that and, while City are appealing, a sizeable sanction may be still to come. Perhaps that is fitting: the title could be decided on the pitch, rather than in the courts. The temptation is to attribute a slide of three defeats and a draw in four games to off-field matters. Enzo Maresca has denied that is a factor , and whatever his players say in the future, that is overly simplistic. Rather, there are similarities with another side who spiralled from a 100 percent start into a wretched run: Liverpool won their first five matches last season, and then lost four in a row, while City began with seven straight victories a year later. In each case, the initial results came with evidence of flaws which did not halt them: until, suddenly, they did. Neither looked solid defensively or always had the right balance in midfield even when winning . In City’s case, Maresca has lamented a lack of clean sheets, with none in their last nine matches in all competitions, with 26 goals already conceded in the campaign. A new manager does not seem to know his best back four. His habit of making half-time substitutions, with nine in the last nine matches, can show a decisiveness or an inability to find the right formula before then. Some of that is understandable, as Maresca gets used to a squad that was revamped in the summer. The Italian started by impressing with his tactical acumen. Three months into the campaign, however, his team look too susceptible to the counter-attack and offer too little control in midfield. Perhaps it is unfair to criticise Maresca for being too over-reliant on Erling Haaland for goals; it should be a broader concern that, beyond Haaland, Elliot Anderson, Iliman Ndiaye and Rayan Cherki , not too many others are enjoying a fine season personally. Maresca returned to the Etihad Stadium aware of pertinent precedents. He has raised the subject of Manchester United after Sir Alex Ferguson and Arsenal after Arsene Wenger . Neither David Moyes nor Unai Emery mounted a title challenge after replacing a legend. When City touched stratospheric heights under Guardiola, there was always the probability they would decline after him, regardless of the scale of their funding, the legitimacy of those funds or the identity of his successor. item.title: Fred Vasseur furious with latest "unprofessional" Ferrari clash: "It's the same speech as Mexico"
item.description: Motorsport photo Ferrari team boss Fred Vasseur says Charles Leclerc's contact with Lewis Hamilton in the Las Vegas Grand Prix was "unacceptable" and showed "lack of respect for the team", with the Formula 1 team set for fresh crisis talks just three weeks after their spat in Mexico. Vasseur had to hold talks with both Leclerc and Hamilton for their costly Mexico skirmish and will do so again after his two cars tangled on the streets of Las Vegas on lap 38, with Leclerc to blame for leaving his front wing dangling on the inside of Hamilton, sending the Briton into a spin. Leclerc received a 10-second penalty for the collision, while Hamilton dropped to 10th and eventually crossed the line in eighth. Leclerc was classified in 10th place after the penalty had been added to his race time. Coming so soon after Mexico, the thought of his drivers tangling again and the prospect of fresh talks to clear the air had worn thin on Vasseur. "Charles, I want to see you at the end of the race, before anything else," Vasseur said on the team radio during the cooldown lap. When asked what that discussion was like, Vasseur tellingly replied: "It was not a discussion. I spoke. "I think he apologised, he understood, but the result is there. You make a mistake, you say: 'My mistake, I'm sorry'. But you [still] made a mistake." Frederic Vasseur, Ferrari Frederic Vasseur, Ferrari He added: "It's unacceptable. It's a lack of respect for the team, for the sponsors, the same speech as after Mexico. I think we had a clear discussion in Sao Paulo. Today it wasn't professional. I think it's probably the escalation of tension." Following complaints from Hamilton, Ferrari had already been in touch with Leclerc about the aggressive way he was squeezing the Briton. Las Vegas' oval-like slipstreaming race required a degree of trust and teamwork for drivers to move through the pack of cars, as not racing each other was not an option either. The race became a painful reminder that trust between Leclerc and Hamilton is absent. "We passed the message to Charles during the race to think about the team when he was fighting in the right way, but you can't freeze the position on this kind of race, because you are in the slipstream," Vasseur explained. "If you slow down, the guy who is behind you is overtaking you. And all the other teams were able to overtake each other 20 times during the race. You can't imagine the frustration for me, but more important for all the guys at home." item.title: Verstappen wins extraordinary race as Ferraris collide
item.description: The Las Vegas Grand Prix featured 'yo-yo racing' throughout the field with regular overtaking [Reuters] Red Bull's Max Verstappen won an extraordinary Las Vegas Grand Prix that featured 34 lead changes in a non-stop battle at the front. The leading group of 10 cars were tied together for the vast majority of the race as the lead constantly changed hands between Verstappen and the Mercedes drivers George Russell and Kimi Antonelli. But Verstappen was the one constant, always seeming a step ahead of his rivals as he debated electrical energy deployment strategy with his team. And in the final laps Mercedes' challenge unravelled as first Russell made a mistake and crashed trying to pass Antonelli, and the Italian lost out to the two McLarens of Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri going into the final lap. The world champion dropped to fifth going on to the Strip on the last lap but was able to reclaim the place from Alpine's Pierre Gasly at the end of the long straight. And there was more drama at Ferrari as Charles Leclerc earned a 10-second penalty for tipping Lewis Hamilton into a spin. Earlier, Hamilton had been given a 10-second penalty of his own for passing Norris off the track in a fight for position that also involved Leclerc. It was a grand prix more reminiscent of American oval racing than Formula 1, and it depended on unique circumstances revolving around the Las Vegas circuit and energy-starved hybrid engines this year. But there was no questioning the showbiz value in the city that prides itself as the entertainment capital of the world. The key stories of an engrossing race were: Verstappen's remarkable intelligence and control in the lead in the most demanding of circumstances Another dip in a dreadful season for Russell More controversy at Ferrari, as both drivers earned 10-second penalties for driving infringements in battles involving the other Verstappen in control despite lead changes Challengers came and went but Max Verstappen was never without the lead for long in Las Vegas [Getty Images] "How many overtakes did I do?" Verstappen asked his engineer on the slowing down lap, as he reflected on a race the like of which F1 has not seen since the famous Monza slipstreaming battles of the 1960s and early 1970s. "Yeah, and not many of them on the straight," his new engineer Tom Hart said, summing up how Verstappen had secured the win against the Mercedes challenge. Lap after lap after lap, Verstappen, who started from pole, would lose the lead to Russell on the Strip only to reclaim it at the last corner, usually going around the outside. If that did not work, and Russell passed later in the lap, or led across the line, Verstappen developed a trademark move around the outside of Turn Three to get back in front. The race went on and on like that, punctuated by a mid-grand prix safety car, but through it all Verstappen always seemed in control. item.title: First-Class degree not enough to make excellent teacher – TRCN
item.description: The Teachers Registration Council of Nigeria (TRCN) says possessing a first-class degree does not automatically make an individual an excellent teacher. Dr. Ronke Soyombo, Registrar/Chief Executive of TRCN, stated this in an interview with Newsmen on Sunday in Abuja. Soyombo stressed the importance of professional competence adding that effective teaching required more than academic qualifications. The registrar explained that teachers must demonstrate competence in five critical areas assessed through the Council’s professional qualifying examination. She identified the areas as basic mathematics, foundational literacy, digital literacy, pedagogy, and safeguarding and child protection. According to her, teachers must possess a sound understanding of basic mathematical concepts to effectively support children’s learning and development. She described foundational literacy as equally important, noting that strong literacy skills enabled teachers to support learning across other subject areas. The registrar said teachers must also understand today’s children, particularly those belonging to the Alpha Generation, and the technological environment in which they operate. She identified digital literacy as the third major area of assessment, describing it as compulsory for teachers seeking to engage effectively with contemporary learners. To illustrate the challenge, Soyombo recalled visiting an examination centre where she encountered an elderly teacher struggling with a computer mouse. “I remember visiting an examination centre recently and meeting an elderly teacher who held a computer mouse and asked me, ‘Madam, what am I going to do with this?’” she said. She said the encounter highlighted the extent of digital literacy challenges confronting some teachers and raised concerns about their preparedness for modern classrooms. “How can teachers effectively engage children in today’s classrooms if they are not comfortable with basic technology?” she asked. Soyombo, however, acknowledged the challenges and disclosed that several training programmes were being implemented to improve teachers’ digital competence. On pedagogy, she said possessing excellent academic qualifications did not automatically translate into the ability to teach effectively. “Having a first-class degree does not automatically make someone an excellent teacher,” she said. She explained that academic qualifications alone could not guarantee that a teacher understood how to apply appropriate instructional methods to address different learning needs. According to her, classrooms comprise learners with varying abilities, including average pupils, children requiring additional support, and gifted and talented learners. She stressed that teachers must possess the pedagogical skills to effectively reach all categories of learners and ensure inclusive classroom experiences. “This is why pedagogy is a critical component of our examination. “Without sound pedagogical skills, a person cannot b

item.title: Zaire Franklin shares unbelievable details of broken leg as Packers await his return
item.description: Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images Green Bay Packers linebacker Zaire Franklin has revealed that he completed two more periods of practice despite suffering a broken leg in what he described as a ‘freak accident’. The defensive captain returned to the field for the first time since fracturing his shin during practice, with his absence leaving a gap in Green Bay’s linebacker unit. Franklin had missed four consecutive games after initially believing the collision was nothing more than a dead leg. However, an X-ray later confirmed the extent of the damage. Zaire Franklin reveals he practised on a broken leg after Green Bay Packers injury Speaking about the incident, Franklin explained how an unusual collision left him with a fracture that he initially struggled to believe. “Somebody just kind of kneed me in a weird way. I’m thinking it’s just dead leg. I actually finished practice. I practiced two more periods on a broken leg,” Franklin said, according to ESPN’s Rob Demovsky. The 30-year-old was stunned when the X-ray revealed the injury, admitting: “And then once I got the X-ray and it was broke, I was looking like, I almost couldn’t believe it. It just looked fake.” Franklin’s injury was particularly frustrating given his previous record of availability. He had missed only one game through injury during his first eight NFL seasons before sitting out four straight contests this season. “The only thing that was going through my mind was, ‘D***, I can’t practice tomorrow?’ It’s been a journey but I’m glad we were able to push through,” he added. “Thank God for keeping my head down and really been leaning on my family. I’m just glad to be back.” Franklin recorded 41 tackles, one forced fumble and one pass defensed in six starts before his injury. He was also named a season-long captain in his first year with Green Bay after holding the same responsibility with the Indianapolis Colts for six consecutive seasons. His return comes at a useful time for the Packers, who have already lost Edgerrin Cooper to a season-ending Achilles injury. Head coach Matt LaFleur expects Franklin to participate on a limited basis, leaving his availability for the Rams clash dependent on how he progresses through the week. item.title: The Daily Hilario: ¡Vamos Republic!
item.description: Nov 21, 2026; Sacramento, CA, USA; Sacramento Republic FC celebrates winning the USL Championship against the Louisville City FC at Sacramento's Heart Health Park. Mandatory Credit: Scott Marshall-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Turned out to be a fun day of sports yesterday … away from the clownshoes of Chelsea that is. The USL Championship game was held yesterday, to determine the winner of America’s second rate soccer league. The league follows the standard US format of a regular season then playoffs, and my local team made it to the final for the second time in their history — a long twelve years after the first time (feels just like yesterday). The fun part about the Championship game is that it’s not at a neutral site, so The Republic got to have home field advantage just like back in 2012. That advantage was sapped a bit by the awkward kick-off time (12pm EST; 9am local) and the freezing temperatures of an early NorCal winter, but an advantage was eventually had. The Republic took the lead and generally dominated the game from start to finish, but the visitors capitalized on a rare error from the captain to equalize and then continued to threaten occasionally on the counter. The only real question was whether they could be broken down. The answer was, no. Thankfully, the penalty shootout swung the home team’s way — Sacramento’s stalvart goalkeeper, Danny Vitiello making two saves and taking Man of the Match honors — and we got to celebrate a second championship for the city. Fireworks and trophy lift in the daytime? Gotta be USL! (Fun fact: the USL have grand plans to establish a new top division to rival MLS, with the added feature of proper promotion/relegation. That’s slated to start in 2028, should it happen. They only have a handful teams committed to it right now, so we’ll see. Sacramento tried to make MLS expansion happen for many years now, but this may be a more feasible route especially with the new soccer-specific stadium being built as we speak .) And the day was still only halfway over! The afternoon brought even more non-Chelsea-sport joy, with the University of Washington taking down the defending national champions, Indiana in a game of collegiate handegg. It’s been a disappointing season for the Huskies overall, with great summer expectations dashed by injuries, questionable coaching decisions, and inconsistent play (including from some of the biggest stars on the team), but this win does put a bit of shine on things as we head into Bowl season. And then, the nightcap was a rather fun F1 race in Las Vegas. With the championship already decided, everybody was out there just having some fun and passing each other left and right. Even Verstappen was enjoying himself. Talk amongst yourselves.

item.title: Paras Mhambrey set to join Punjab Kings as bowling coach
item.description: MUMBAI: Former India and Mumbai Indians bowling coach Paras Mhambrey is set to join Punjab Kings as their new bowling coach for IPL-2027, TOI has learnt. Punjab Kings had parted ways with their bowling coach James Hopes recently. Mhambrey will thus chalk out bowling strategies with PBKS head coach Ricky Ponting and skipper Shreyas Iyer. "Paras has signed a contract with Punjab Kings today," a source told TOI. Mhambrey will thus be the second man from MI to join Punjab Kings after Hardik Pandya, who came to the Chandigarh-based franchise through a high-profile trade. Mhambrey recently parted ways with MI after a long association with the franchise. Mhambrey, who was India's bowling coach from 2022 to 2024 under head coach Rahul Dravid, has had two stints with MI. He was initially with MI since the IPL’s inception in 2008, and then rejoined MI after completing his tenure with the Indian team following the 2024 T20 World Cup triumph. Mhambrey is currently in Dubai as bowling coach of MI Emirates in the ILT20. He had also coached the India Under-19 team in the 2020 U-19 World Cup in South Africa. During his nearly three-year stint with Team India, the 54-year-old ex-India pacer-turned coach was credited by many, especially ace pacer Mohammed Shami, who kept gesturing towards him from the field during matches, for the Indian bowlers’ brilliant show in the 2023 ODI World Cup in India, and the T20 World Cup in West Indies in June this year. The Mumbaikar is a product of the BCA-Mafatlal bowling scheme under England fast bowling great Frank Tyson in 1990. He then went on to possess a rich 21-year coaching experience in his CV, a period in which he coached multiple domestic teams, including Bengal, Baroda, Maharashtra and Vidarbha.

item.title: Sharks Locker Room: What’s “Mature” Hockey? Celebrini Loses His Voice
item.description: The San Jose Sharks…are in the playoffs? The Sharks are third in the Pacific, after a 4-3 win over the Seattle Kraken: Michael Misa , Nolan Allan, Macklin Celebrini , and Ivar Stenberg scored. Of course, take being in the playoffs as of now with a massive grain of salt. San Jose plays, once again, in the weakest division in hockey. Their .480 Points % is well behind the Utah Mammoth’s .563. The Central squad owns the final wild card berth in the West. Also, all the Pacific teams chasing them have games in hand: The Anaheim Ducks and Calgary Flames each have one, and the Kraken have five. But to their credit, the Sharks have grabbed nine points out of their last 12, turning around a season that looked like it was on the verge of spiraling out of control. Hasso here today, nice win for the owner — Sheng Peng (@Sheng_Peng) November 22, 2026 After the game, Ryan Warsofsky spoke on trusting his fourth line to close the game and his definition of “mature” hockey, Celebrini praised Dmitry Orlov ’s power play work, Misa shared what the San Jose Sharks took from a week of hard practices, and Orlov gave the praise back to his captain. A deeper game story with micro-stats from Stathletes and game action clips, Sharks Insight, will be published soon. Ryan Warsofsky Warsofsky, on Sharks always turning to Orlov on the power play, in the end: Just a calming influence. He understands what’s in front of him. He can make those reads, and he knows when to shoot it. Makes a nice play to Mack, but also makes a nice play shooting it to the net when we have two guys there. Warsofsky, on San Jose Sharks’ third period: I liked our third a lot. I thought it was a mature third. They couldn’t get the goalie pulled, but we were forechecking still. We weren’t on our heels. Warsofsky, on what “mature” hockey is: Making them come 200 feet, not giving them chances, not handing them chances. There’s a lot of different situations. There’s puck play through the neutral zone. There’s, you know you’re late in your shift and [don’t] try to make the extra play. That’s putting it behind their defense to make them turn. That’s just a simple brand of hockey. That’s winning hockey that every coach talks about and just having understanding of playing on the defensive side of things and you’ll get offense from that and you just got to believe in that. Warsofsky, on relying on fourth line to close win: They were playing really good hockey. They were forechecking. They were skating. They had great detail in their game. They earned those minutes. I thought [Leason] was really good, smart. Makes a really good read in the third period that us coaches really appreciate. The average fan may not see it but just works to get above and takes away time and space. So thought he came in and gave us some good legs. item.title: Georgia’s 34-6 Blowout of South Carolina Ends With Ugly Postgame Scene
item.description: COLUMBIA, SOUTH CAROLINA - NOVEMBER 21: Head coach Kirby Smart of the Georgia Bulldogs waves his hat as he walks off the field after defeating the South Carolina Gamecocks at Williams-Brice Stadium on November 21, 2026 in Columbia, South Carolina. (Photo by Jacob Kupferman/Getty Images) Getty COLUMBIA, SOUTH CAROLINA - NOVEMBER 21: Gunner Stockton #14 of the Georgia Bulldogs passes the ball in the first half against the South Carolina Gamecocks during their game at Williams-Brice Stadium on November 21, 2026 in Columbia, South Carolina. (Photo by Jacob Kupferman/Getty Images) Getty The Georgia Bulldogs made quite the statement Saturday, dominating No. 21 South Carolina in a 34-6 victory that left little doubt about which team was better. However, the action apparently wasn’t finished when the final whistle sounded, as a heated exchange between players created an unexpected scene following Georgia’s impressive performance. Georgia had already taken care of business on the field, but tensions between the two SEC programs reportedly spilled over afterward. According to WSB-TV sports reporter Alison Mastrangelo, a South Carolina player was seen exchanging words with Georgia players before coaches from both teams intervened to prevent the situation from escalating. “Brief scuffle after the game, a South Carolina player doing a lot of chirping to some of the Georgia players after the game. Coaches from both teams broke it up pretty quickly,” Mastrangelo reported [see video here]. Georgia’s Dominant Victory Takes Unexpected Turn After Final Whistle The confrontation added an unusual ending to a game that Georgia largely controlled. The Bulldogs scored 31 unanswered points against South Carolina, turning what could have been a competitive SEC matchup into another convincing performance. For Georgia, the victory was about much more than defeating a conference opponent. The Bulldogs also secured a spot in the SEC Championship Game, giving their fans another reason to celebrate as the regular season approaches its conclusion. Getty COLUMBIA, SOUTH CAROLINA – NOVEMBER 21: Gunner Stockton #14 of the Georgia Bulldogs passes the ball in the first half against the South Carolina Gamecocks during their game at Williams-Brice Stadium on November 21, 2026 in Columbia, South Carolina. (Photo by Jacob Kupferman/Getty Images) However, the postgame exchange quickly became another talking point. While Mastrangelo described the incident as brief, the fact that coaches from both programs needed to step in suggests emotions remained high even after the outcome had been decided. There is an important distinction between players exchanging heated words and an altercation becoming something more serious. Based on the initial account, the situation was brought under control quickly, and there was no indication that it developed into a prolonged confrontation. item.title: Robert Griffin III worries UCLA could get ‘screwed’ by CFP selection committee
item.description: Bob Donnan-Imagn Images Robert Griffin III worries UCLA could get ‘screwed’ by CFP selection committee appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . UCLA football ’s undefeated streak finally came to an end on Saturday as the No. 4-ranked Bruins suffered a 18-16 triple-overtime loss to Michigan. The defeat dropped UCLA to 10-1 overall and 7-1 in Big Ten play, but former Baylor star Robert Griffin III is particularly concerned about the Bruins’ College Football Playoff chances. The timing of UCLA’s first defeat could make the situation even more frustrating. Starting quarterback Ty Dieffenbach, who took over the starting role after Nico Iamaleava suffered a season-ending injury, was carted off the field during the first overtime period in Saturday’s game. Dieffenbach’s injury left the Bruins without their starting signal-caller. In an X post, Griffin III warned that UCLA could be unfairly disadvantaged by the CFP selection committee despite putting together a playoff-worthy season because of their starting quarterbacks’ injury. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “UCLA is in prime position to get screwed by the CFP selection committee because they won’t have their starting QB or their backup QB despite their season being worthy of a playoff spot,” Griffin wrote. Meanwhile, Kyle Whittingham secured his biggest victory as Michigan’s head coach with an impressive statement win. The Wolverines improved to 6-5 overall and secured bowl eligibility with a memorable performance in front of their home crowd. The victory also marked Michigan’s first win as an unranked team against a ranked opponent since its back-to-back victories over No. 2 Ohio State and No. 11 Alabama to close out the 2024 season. With UCLA falling to Michigan, three of the Big Ten’s four highest-ranked teams suffered losses this weekend. No. 8 Indiana and No. 14 Ohio State also endured road losses. The 10-1 Bruins will now turn their attention to an important matchup against 8-3 USC next week at the Rose Bowl. A victory would secure UCLA a berth in the Big Ten Championship Game and likely strengthen its chances of reaching the College Football Playoff . However, another loss could potentially eliminate the Bruins from both opportunities after their 10-0 start to the season. item.title: This is excellent from Pat Nevin who was inside St James’ Park on Saturday night
item.description: Newcastle United and Arsenal players walk out onto the St. James' Park pitch ahead of their Premier League fixture. Pat Nevin sees a lot of Newcastle United. The former Chelsea and Everton winger a regular visitor at St James’ Park. Pat Nevin often on media duties at United matches. As a result of that, he has far more of a clue than your average pundit about Newcastle United, the good an the bad. The one-time player was once again on media duties at St James’ Park on Saturday night for the Newcastle United 2 Arsenal 2 match. As is usually a case, his reaction to what he witnessed was pretty spot on. Pat Nevin on BBC Radio Five Live, commenting on the first half moment when Bruno Guimaraes almost headed Arsenal into the lead: “That would have broken a few hearts around here, a great run from Bruno Guimaraes. A very deep header, he’s a deep-lying midfielder. These Newcastle fans have watched him so many times in black and white and that was a decent half-chance.” Pat Nevin after Eze gave Arsenal a 33rd minute lead: “You felt as though it was coming. The Newcastle midfielders pushed up further and the second they did so, they were shredded. That pass from Kai Havertz is an absolute delight, he’s such a special player. Eberechi Eze lashed it past goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek.” Pat Nevin commenting after Harvey Barnes equalised four minutes after the break: “Newcastle have been fabulous at the start of the second half. They’ve closed down higher up the field, not giving Arsenal any time on the ball. They’ve struggled to be able to zip the ball about like they did in the first. But can Newcastle keep this up?” Malick Thiaw giving United a 2-1 lead, Pat Nevin: “Beyond amazing. There is not a Newcastle fan in this ground who could see this coming. They have come out with such a brilliant attitude in the second half. Dan Burn at the back post with nobody on him. Malick Thiaw has the easiest tap-in in the world.” Pat Nevin as the match moves into the nine minutes of added time and the score 2-2, Noni Madueke having equalised on 78 minutes: “This has got the feeling of a cup tie. I love that Newcastle don’t want to settle just for a point against the champions. But I think they’re running out of players, Lewis Hall has sat down.” Pat Nevin with a perfect summing up after the final whistle: “Isn’t it a joy when you think you know what’s going on in football but you know nothing at half-time. In the first half Arsenal were all over Newcastle, there was not one area where Arsenal were not better. Then three changes at half time and Newcastle were superb in the second half and the fans will be wondering where that has been all season? A great performance coming back after being a goal down. They showed the capabilities they’ve got.”

item.title: Julian Sayin May Have Played Last Game at Ohio State
item.description: LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 31: Julian Sayin #10 of the Ohio State Buckeyes walks out of the tunnel before the game against the USC Trojans at Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum on October 31, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. Yes, Jeremiah Smith is likely to leave, and that changes the passing attack considerably. Sayin is still a special talent, though, and Ohio State should be one of the best teams in the country next year if Sayin is on the field. He also can potentially push to b

item.title: Boost for Barcelona as Premier League forward prefers Camp Nou move over Arsenal, PSG
item.description: Boost for Barcelona as Premier League forward prefers Camp Nou move over Arsenal, PSG According to French outlet Foot Sur7 (h/t SPORT ), Barcelona could have an advantage in the race for AFC Bournemouth striker Eli Junior Kroupi as he prefers a move to the Catalan club over Arsenal and Paris Saint-Germain. The 20-year-old starlet has attracted growing interest following his development in the Premier League, with Barça having had monitored him since last summer. The likes of Arsenal and PSG have also shown a strong interest in the French international. But, as per the report, Kroupi is particularly keen on the possibility of wearing the Blaugrana shirt if he were to leave Bournemouth. Barcelona see Kroupi as a potential long-term attacking option As mentioned earlier, Barcelona have already monitored the Frenchman’s progress, having followed him during last summer’s transfer window. Having parted ways with Robert Lewandowski and Ferran Torres, the Catalans were in the market for a new centre-forward and saw Kroupi as an alternative to their priority target, Julian Alvarez. Barcelona continue to monitor Kroupi. (Photo by Gareth Cattermole/Getty Images) An injury in the summer derailed any hopes of a move, though, while the La Liga champions roped in Gabriel Jesus as a short-term, cost-effective solution. As such, Kroupi’s name remains on sporting director Deco’s list of possible targets for a future reinforcement of the forward line. Given his age, versatility, and goalscoring ability, Barcelona see him as a potential long-term option to lead their attacking unit. Bournemouth’s position on Kroupi For now, Bournemouth have no intention of allowing Kroupi to leave during the January transfer window and consider him an important part of their sporting project. The Cherries are also in a strong negotiating position because his contract runs until June 2030, giving them considerable control over his future. Kroupi would prefer Barcelona over Arsenal and PSG. (Photo by Catherine Steenkeste/Getty Images) Kroupi, for his part, wants to rediscover his best form this season before making a decision about his next move. As such, the summer transfer window could become the more realistic moment to assess his options, with reports in England suggesting that Bournemouth could demand a fee approaching £100 million for the youngster. Such a valuation, though, could make negotiations particularly difficult for Barcelona, given their economic limitations, compared to the likes of Arsenal and PSG, who have greater financial resources available. But, Kroupi’s preference towards the Blaugrana would give Deco an important advantage in any future negotiations.

item.title: Massimiliano Allegri reveals quirky secret to Napoli's gritty win and explains Scott McTominay masterstroke
item.description: SSC Napoli v Torino FC - Serie A 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Napoli manager Massimiliano Allegri has opened up about the unconventional psychological approach he used to inspire his side during their hard-fought 1-0 win against Torino on Saturday. After a frustrating first half at the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona, the veteran tactician urged his players to change their emotional outlook to break the deadlock. The power of a positive mindset Napoli secured a vital three points thanks to a solitary strike from Scott McTominay, but the story behind the goal was as much about mentality as it was about technique. Allegri revealed that he sensed a heavy atmosphere among his players during the interval after they failed to convert several early openings. The manager decided that a shift in mood was necessary to unlock the opposition's stubborn defensive line. "It was as if the right mood wasn't there, because we had several favourable chances without scoring," the coach explained to Sky Sport Italia . "So I said to the team: 'Guys, let's smile: maybe we can manage to score a goal.' Winning a match with a bit of suffering was useful for us, but we still need to improve in certain situations, such as managing the ball at the end. However, we were very good at defending set pieces. In the past, we lacked the nastiness in defending that we saw today." Tactical shifts and McTominay's role While the psychological element played its part, Allegri also had to navigate a tactical puzzle following an early injury to Antonio Vergara. After initially introducing Kevin De Bruyne in a support role behind Rasmus Hojlund, the manager decided to swap positions between the Belgian and Scott McTominay. This adjustment proved to be the turning point as the Scottish international began to cause significant problems for the Torino backline from a more advanced starting position. "The tactical changes? It's also the fun part of this job," Allegri noted. "I thought De Bruyne in the hole could do better, then I moved McTominay closer to Hojlund because we needed a bit more there. But I told McTominay not to be found in a vertical position behind Hojlund, but to get there, because that way he would be less markable. When I put him there he went, but stayed still, then in the second half he moved more between the lines and was much better." Defending Rasmus Hojlund's form Despite the win being secured by a midfielder, Allegri was quick to jump to the defence of Hojlund. The Danish forward worked tirelessly throughout the contest but failed to find the back of the net himself, leading to questions about his current confidence levels. Allegri dismissed any suggestions that the former Manchester United man is struggling or needs special treatment to find his goalscoring touch again. "Hojlund needs to be recovered? It's absolutely not like that," the Napoli boss. "He played a good game, making himself available to the team. He had several chances and is very useful and important fo

item.title: Full list: FG announces 19 international job vacancies [How to apply]
item.description: The Federal Government, FG has announced 19 international job vacancies for qualified Nigerians at the African Space Agency and the General Secretariat of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC). The vacancies, announced by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, comprise five positions at the African Space Agency headquarters in Cairo, Egypt, and 14 positions at the OIC headquarters in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia. The ministry disclosed this in two separate vacancy announcements dated Friday, November 20, 2026, signed by its spokesperson, Oluwafemi Adeniyi, and shared on its official Facebook page on Saturday. According to the ministry, the African Space Agency is recruiting for five positions, with application deadlines of November 25 and December 10, 2026. The positions include Director, Corporate Services (D-1); Director-General, African Space Agency (D-2); Head of Legal Affairs (Grade P-5); Senior Finance Officer (P3); and Senior Human Resources Officer (P3). The ministry said interested and qualified Nigerians should visit the agency’s official website at https://africanspaceagency.org for details of the eligibility requirements and application procedures. For the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation, the ministry announced 14 vacancies across its departments and specialised units. The positions include Director-General of Political Affairs; Director, Administration Department; Director, Information Department; Director, Conference Department; Director, Muslim Communities and Minorities; Director, African Affairs; and Director, European Affairs and International Organisations. Others are Head of Human Resources (PP2); Professional Officer, Human Resources (PP2); Professional Officers, Administration Department (P2); Director, Peace, Security and Mediation Unit; Chief of HRC Office – IUT; Registrar – IUT; and Deputy Internal Auditor – IUT. The ministry said the application deadlines for the OIC positions range from November 29 to December 24, 2026. It urged interested and qualified Nigerians to visit the organisation’s official vacancy portal at https://www.oic-oci.org/en/vacancies for information on the specific requirements, application procedures and deadlines for each position. How to apply Interested Nigerians can apply through the following official platforms: African Space Agency: Visit https://africanspaceagency.org , navigate to the recruitment or careers section, and check the available positions, eligibility criteria and application instructions. Organisation of Islamic Cooperation: Visit https://www.oic-oci.org/en/vacancies , select the relevant vacancy and follow the stated application procedure. Applicants are advised to review the requirements for their preferred positions and submit their applications before the respective deadlines. item.title: How every post-Ferguson Man United boss began their reign ahead of Pochettino's debut
item.description: How every post-Ferguson Man United boss began their reign ahead of Pochettino's debut Mauricio Pochettino begins his reign as Manchester United manager at Liverpool this afternoon. Pochettino has become Manchester United's eighth permanent manager since Sir Alex Ferguson's retirement in 2013, and the third in the last three seasons. The Argentine has been tasked with leading the Red Devils out of the Premier League relegation places, but faces a tough first examination at Anfield. Ahead of his debut, here is how each of Manchester United's post-Ferguson managers did on their first game as permanent manager. David Moyes Manchester United 2-0 Wigan Athletic (Community Shield, 2013) David Moyes was dubbed 'The Chosen One' after being handpicked by Ferguson as his replacement. Moyes's impressive work at Everton over more than a decade had earned him the role and he started with trophy success in the Community Shield . Robin van Persie scored both goals as the Red Devils beat surprise FA Cup winners Wigan at Wembley. Moyes was sacked after only 10 months in charge, with the defending Premier League champions seventh in the table with four games to go. Louis van Gaal Manchester United 1-2 Swansea City (Premier League, 2014) Manchester United sought a proven winner to replace Moyes, as Louis van Gaal arrived at Old Trafford. A seven-time title winner across three different leagues, Van Gaal's reign began with defeat. Swansea stunned Manchester United to hand the Red Devils their first home defeat on the opening day of the league season since 1972. It was also the first time that Swansea had won a league game at Old Trafford. Van Gaal spent two seasons with the club and won the FA Cup is second campaign, but was dismissed as United turned to Jose Mourinho . Jose Mourinho Manchester United 2-1 Leicester City (Community Shield, 2016) Jose Mourinho took the reins from Van Gaal and began in trademark Mourinho fashion, with a trophy. Summer signing Zlatan Ibrahimovic scored the winner as Manchester United beat Leicester City to win the Community Shield. United won the League Cup and Europa League during Mourinho's first season, but it proved to be a false dawn in terms of silverware success. Ole Gunnar Solskjaer Manchester United 2-1 Watford (Premier League, 2019) In need of stability after the Mourinho era ended in toxic fashion, former favourite Ole Gunnar Solskjaer took charge on an interim basis. A 5-1 thrashing of Cardiff in his first game started a brilliant spell, which earned Solskjaer the permanent position. The Norwegian's first game as permanent manager was a 2-1 win over Watford, with Marcus Rashford and Anthony Martial on target. Erik ten Hag Manchester United 1-2 Brighton (Premier League, 2022) Erik ten Hag had a debut to forget as Pascal Gross' first-half double saw Brighton beat Manchester United at Old Trafford. The German scored both goals as the Seagulls stunned the home side. Ten Hag won trophies in each of his two full seasons at the helm

item.title: Lewis Hamilton: With No. 1 driver backing, we could have beaten Kimi Antonelli to F1 title
item.description: Motorsport photo Seven-time Formula 1 champion Lewis Hamilton believes he could have beaten Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli in their battle earlier in the season had he been given more support from Ferrari . The Briton was speaking after the Las Vegas Grand Prix, where he had another clash with his team-mate Charles Leclerc , which sent him into a spin. He recovered to finish seventh , while Leclerc was penalised and finished 10th. Asked about 1996 F1 champion Damon Hill's suggestion that Ferrari should make him its number one driver, Hamilton said he had never asked for that status, but felt he had needed it earlier in the year. "I've never asked to be number one. I genuinely haven't ever asked," Hamilton said. He pointed to a stage of the season when he was well clear of Leclerc and the nearest driver to challenge Antonelli for the title. "I was second for a long time in the year, and at that point I needed backing to make sure we beat Kimi. There were a few circumstances in the season where, with the support, we could have beaten Kimi," he said. After the 41-year-old claimed his first grand prix win with Ferrari in Barcelona in June, he was second in the drivers' standings , 41 points behind Antonelli and 40 points ahead of Leclerc. He was also second after Monaco, Belgium and Hungary. Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari, Charles Leclerc, Ferrari Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari, Charles Leclerc, Ferrari Antonelli went on to secure the championship at the Mexican Grand Prix, one week before Mercedes won the constructors' title, and now has 402 points to Hamilton's 267. "I don't know, but it's not something I want to get into," he said when asked where his relationship with his team-mate goes from here. "These are questions that people are asking. At the end of the day, I performed as hard as I could, and I've been giving everything I could to get those points today. "We were just constantly hit with challenges, and I just kept my head down." Earlier in the race, Hamilton had been handed a 10-second penalty for leaving the track and gaining an advantage over McLaren's Lando Norris . "10 seconds was insane and very, very harsh," he continued. "I was avoiding colliding with them, and they could have just told me to give the place back. A 10-second [penalty] is nuts. But I came back and I got back into the fight, and I could see Max up ahead and I was like, we're back in the fight. "I was fighting with McLaren , so I honestly thought that I could maybe fight for a podium, and I'm literally only thinking about fighting McLaren, because that's where we need to be to get the second." To read more Motorsport.com articles visit our website .

item.title: ‘Congratulations on the Promotion,’ ‘Go Get the Next One’ — Fans React As Raiders’ Fernando Mendoza Reviews His First NFL Start on LinkedIn
item.description: Nov 15, 2026; Paradise, Nevada, USA; Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza (15) shakes hands with Seattle Seahawks quarterback Drew Lock (2) after the game at Allegiant Stadium. © Gary A. Vasquez-Imagn Images Fernando Mendoza is embracing the learning curve that comes with becoming the Las Vegas Raiders’ starting quarterback. After his first career NFL start against the Seattle Seahawks, the rookie took to LinkedIn to reflect on it, and fans had a lot to say. Mendoza made the start in Week 10 as the Raiders hosted Seattle at Allegiant Stadium. Las Vegas lost 21-13, but Mendoza focused on what he could take from the experience instead of the result. Fans Celebrate Fernando Mendoza’s “Promotion” on LinkedIn Mendoza used the post to reflect on moving into the starting role and to thank the people who supported him. “Promoted… A lot to learn from my first NFL start,” Mendoza wrote . “Grateful for my family, friends, and Raider Nation for the support! Looking forward to getting better and earning the trust of my teammates and coaches every day.” The rookie also shared two photos from the game, one of himself on the field and another of him celebrating with teammates. Mendoza’s post drew a wave of supportive messages, with several fans congratulating the 23-year-old on his first NFL start. “Congrats on the promotion, you deserved it,” one user wrote , adding a smiling-face emoji. Another fan encouraged him to keep it up, saying , “Go get ’em! Keep making our Raider Nation proud!” SET YOUR LINEUPS: PFN’s Free Fantasy Start/Sit Optimizer Others were already looking ahead. One supporter commented , “We’re expecting big things, Mr. Mendoza,” alongside a GIF of Luke Skywalker from “Star Wars.” Mendoza’s choice of platform also caught the attention of some fans. “The king LinkedIn didn’t know that it needed. Love that there is no ghostwriter,” one fan commented . Another fan quipped , “Congrats on the promotion without a salary increase!” “Congrats on your first start, Fernando! I like that your first thought was what you could learn from it. Go get the next one,” another user remarked . BE THE GM OF YOUR FAVORITE TEAM: PFN’s Free NFL Mock Draft Simulator Mendoza still has plenty of work ahead as he prepares for his next start. The rookie completed 17 of 29 passes for 143 yards against Seattle, but the Seahawks’ pass rush made for a tough afternoon, taking him down six times in the 21-13 win. “All of those sacks were on me,” he later said . “I believe the offensive line played great, and I’m excited to get back out there this next Sunday.” Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak said the coaching staff needs to do more to help the rookie adjust to his bigger role. The next test comes quickly against a Denver Broncos defense that ranks No. 7 with a PFN Defense Impact Score of 81.0. item.title: ‘That Is a Stunning Number,’ ‘Deserved Punishment’ — Analysts React As ESPN Loses 7 Million Paid TV Subscribers in Just 1 Year
item.description: ‘That Is a Stunning Number,’ ‘Deserved Punishment’ — Analysts React As ESPN Loses 7 Million Paid TV Subscribers in Just 1 Year ESPN’s pay-TV subscriber base keeps shrinking. The network lost approximately 7 million subscribers in a year, according to Disney’s annual report, which puts ESPN and ESPN2 at 54 million pay-TV subscribers each, down from 61 million a year earlier. That is roughly half of the 100 million-plus ESPN had at its 2011 peak. Awful Announcing reported the latest figures Thursday, and they quickly got sports media personalities talking. Some were stunned by the size of the drop, while others questioned ESPN’s programming choices and whether its push into streaming can turn things around. Sports Media Voices React to ESPN’s Subscriber Drop Disney filed the report with the Securities and Exchange Commission on Tuesday. It covers the fiscal year that ended Oct. 3 and bases the subscriber counts on Nielsen Media Research estimates as of September 2026. The filing says ESPN’s subscription revenue depends on how many people access its channels through cable, satellite and other TV providers, as well as how many subscribe to its streaming services. ESPN also offers its own ESPN Select and ESPN Unlimited plans, while some of its content is available to Disney+ subscribers through a dedicated ESPN section. Awful Announcing report , written by Matt Yoder, noted that ESPN found an investor in the NFL through an equity deal and that Disney has been adding more ESPN content to Disney+. The drop works out to roughly 11.5% of the network’s pay-TV subscribers in a single year. Toronto Star writer Jonah Sigel focused on the 7 million figure. “That is a stunning number,” he wrote . Anthony Bellino of “760 WJR” kept his reaction even shorter : “Color me shocked.” Not everyone focused on the numbers. Some took aim at what ESPN is selling. The network launched its Unlimited plan last year, and Disney’s filing says it carries every ESPN-branded TV channel along with the ESPN Select content. PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor “America, Actually” host Astead Wesley Herndon minced no words. “Deserved punishment for ESPN Unlimited. They’ve been scamming tennis/soccer fans for a year,” he wrote . Zack Hochberg, a digital media coordinator for QU Sports News, offered the closest thing to a defense of the network in the group. “ESPN is the best company in the world, in my opinion, for live sports. However, there is absolutely zero reason to ever turn on ESPN for anything else. They have completely lost the plot on what consumers want to see,” Hochberg remarked . Brice Larson of 98.3 The Utah ESPN Radio Network came at it as a viewer. item.title: ‘I Sat Behind the Bench for the Same Reason’ — Mark Cuban Backs Colts Owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon Amid Backlash Over Sideline Presence
item.description: Indianapolis Colts principal owner and CEO Carlie Irsay-Gordon. An NFL owner watching a game from the sideline is unusual, especially when that owner carries a headset and takes notes throughout the action. Indianapolis Colts owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon has faced criticism for making that approach part of her game-day routine. The reaction grew louder after Indianapolis’ loss to the Houston Texans. But former Dallas Mavericks majority owner Mark Cuban sees a reason for her to stay involved. Mark Cuban Defends Colts Owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon’s Sideline Presence Cuban backed Irsay-Gordon after former NFL offensive lineman Mitchell Schwartz defended her on X. Schwartz had responded to a clip from the Colts’ 26-3 loss to the Texans on Nov. 19, which showed Irsay-Gordon wearing a headset and writing in a notebook near the team’s sideline. Schwartz rejected the claim that her presence amounted to micromanagement. He argued that she was listening to the coaches’ communications and observing rather than interfering with their work. “I do not get all the hate. She stays out of the way, she listens to the headsets, and she takes notes. In this case she looks up and the coach is nearby and she goes further down the sideline. Mark Cuban sat right behind the bench for half a century and no one batted an eye,” Schwartz wrote. Cuban reshared the post and explained why he spent so much time near the Mavericks’ bench during his 23 years as owner. He compared the practice to attending sales and technology meetings at his companies, where observing employees helped him understand how people worked together. “I sat behind the bench for the same reason I sat in on sales and tech meetings. So I could learn. Watching how people interacted. How they responded to the good and bad and each other. Developing closer relationships,” Cuban wrote on X. He added that being present helped employees feel comfortable approaching him instead of viewing him as a distant executive. It also allowed him to hear exchanges between referees, coaches, and players, giving him information that could help with decisions. Cuban praised Irsay-Gordon for following a similar approach despite the criticism. “Good for her for being an owner that cares enough to not care what other people think,” he wrote. He also corrected Schwartz’s claim about his time near the Mavericks’ bench, noting that it was 23 years, not half a century. PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor Irsay-Gordon has previously explained that she uses the headset to follow play calls, learn more about football, and hold staff accountable. She has even joked that her understanding of the game is at a “fifth-grade reading level.” The criticism has grown alongside Indianapolis’ difficult season and several front-office decisions. The Colts fired longtime general manager Chris Ballard in October, traded veterans Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner, then waived quarterback Daniel Jones after the Houston loss. Irsay-Gordo

item.title: 'It wasn't our best display!' - Ferran Torres reveals why late Nice winner eased Paris Saint-Germain's post-break nerves
item.description: FBL-FRA-LIGUE1-NICE-PSG - AFP Ferran Torres netted a decisive late goal as Paris Saint-Germain edged OGC Nice 3-2 to claim a 12th consecutive victory across all competitions. Speaking after the match, the forward explained why banking three points immediately after the international break mattered more than a fluent performance. Torres clinches vital PSG win on Cote d'Azur Ferran Torres scored with five minutes of normal time remaining to seal a 3-2 victory for Paris Saint-Germain away to OGC Nice, stretching Luis Enrique's side to 12 straight wins in all competitions. The result ended Nice's unbeaten home record this season and opened a five-point cushion over second-placed Lille at the top of Ligue 1. Although Mohamed Amoura put Nice ahead in the eighth minute against the run of play, PSG turned the game around before half-time through Senny Mayulu and Desire Doue. Torres then delivered a deft finish from an Ousmane Dembele pass to give Paris breathing space before Ali Abdi pulled one back in stoppage time. Torres stresses priority of winning after break Despite Nice threatening on the counter-attack during a tense second half, PSG stayed patient until Torres applied the finishing touch. After the final whistle, Torres underlined that grinding out results right after an international break remains vital for dressing-room calm . "This was a very important win," Torres said. "It wasn't our best display, but ultimately, we were competitive and got the three points, and now, we'll focus on the Champions League. It's always important to win, especially after an international break, as it puts the team at ease. Ultimately, we got the three points, which is our priority." How PSG weathered the storm at Nice Nice took the lead with their first chance on a counter-attack through Amoura and stayed compact defensively for much of the opening half-hour. PSG finally broke through on the half-hour mark when Mayulu converted a penalty after Xavier Mandza handled inside the box, before Doue tapped in from Achraf Hakimi's pass less than a minute later. After the break, Joao Neves controlled midfield tempo and PSG pressed aggressively to limit Nice's threat on Matvey Safonov's goal. Hakimi missed a 61st-minute chance to extend the lead before Torres stepped up late on to make the difference. Champions League focus next for Paris With three hard-earned points secured in their first fixture back since a 1-0 win over Troyes two weeks earlier, Torres and his team-mates can now turn their attention to European action. Staying top of Ligue 1 by five points gives PSG a strong platform as they shift focus toward the Champions League.

item.title: SEC standings update: Who is playing Georgia in Atlanta?
item.description: Stop me if you have heard this one before: Georgia is heading back to Atlanta for a shot at the SEC Championship. With a dominant 34-6 rout of South Carolina on Saturday night, Kirby Smart and the Bulldogs punched their ticket to the title game for a record sixth consecutive season. But who will the Bulldogs take on? That is a little harder to break down. If the SEC is the toughest conference in college football, Georgia has routinely been the best of the best. A berth in the title game this year carries a little more significance. Since the playoff is expanding to 24 teams, most believe all major conferences will do away with title games. Sitting comfortably at 8-1 in league play and 10-1 overall on a four-game winning streak, Georgia has already done its part. Now the Bulldogs get to sit back and watch the chaos unfold behind them. And a show it will be. A three-way logjam behind the Bulldogs Behind one-loss Georgia sits a crowded trio of two-loss contenders: Alabama, Tennessee, and Texas. All three are knotted at 6-2 in conference play and 9-2 overall. Oklahoma sits a step back at 5-3, while Florida and Kentucky are both at 5-4, leaving the race for second place strictly between the Tide, Volunteers, and Longhorns. On the surface, sorting out three teams shouldn’t be this messy. But thanks to conference realignment, it is. In the SEC’s expanded era, the schedule creates a massive wrinkle: Alabama, Tennessee, and Texas did not all play one another this season. That means if all three finish tied at 7-2 next weekend, head-to-head results get thrown right out the window, handing the keys to Atlanta over to an odd tiebreaking formula. How Tennessee punches its ticket For Tennessee, the mission starts with taking care of business against a 1-7 Vanderbilt team in a rivalry game. If the Volunteers handle the Commodores and both Texas and Alabama stumble in their rivalry games, Tennessee finishes in sole possession of second place at 7-2 and heads to Atlanta with no math required. Easy. The Vols also have a clean two-team tiebreaker path. Even if Alabama takes care of Auburn, a Tennessee win paired with a Texas loss to Texas A&M leaves the Vols and Crimson Tide tied for second at 7-2. In that scenario, Tennessee gets the nod thanks to its head-to-head win over Alabama earlier this season. Why Texas holds the inside track Texas enters rivalry week riding a five-game winning streak and holding the most enviable position of the three contenders. A victory over 1-7 Texas A&M puts the Longhorns in the driver’s seat. Even if Tennessee beats Vanderbilt, Texas clinches its spot as long as Alabama drops the Iron Bowl. Because the Longhorns defeated the Volunteers earlier this season, a two-way tie between Texas and Tennessee sends the Burnt Orange to Atlanta. Alabama’s narrowing path to Atlanta Alabama, riding a four-game winning streak of its own, has a much tougher road to Atlanta.
